accepted.scope: It is not using physical force and not a disease striking the body; it means speaking or writing against someone.
examples: The report attacked the company for wasting public money.
She attacked the idea in a long blog post.
branchCoverage: attack in speech or writing -> criticize someone or something very strongly in speech or writing
accepted.lemmaPartition: attack (3 senses in this batch): noun = very strong criticism (attack%1:10:00::); verb = to use weapons or force against someone or a place (attack%2:33:00::); verb = to criticize someone very strongly in words (attack%2:32:00::).

accepted.definition: being talented through inherited qualities
accepted.simpleMeaning: having a natural skill that seems to come from your family or from the moment you came into the world.
accepted.scope: It is not the plain sense of coming into the world at a time or place; it describes a skill that seems to be part of a person from the start.
examples: She is a born teacher and can explain anything clearly.
Their daughter is a born performer and loves being on stage.
branchCoverage: being talented through inherited qualities -> having a natural skill that seems to come from your family or from the moment you came into the world

accepted.definition: expletives used informally as intensifiers
accepted.simpleMeaning: used in informal speech before a noun to show anger or strong feeling.
accepted.scope: It is not a curse asking God to punish someone and not a religious judgement; here it only adds force to what you are saying.
examples: I can't get this damn door open.
Where did I put that damn key?
branchCoverage: expletives used informally as intensifiers -> declared usage label (informal swear word used to add force)

accepted.definition: derive or receive pleasure from; get enjoyment from; take pleasure in
accepted.simpleMeaning: to get pleasure from something.
accepted.scope: It is not the formal sense of having the use or benefit of something, as in 'enjoy good health'; it means feeling happy because of an activity or experience.
examples: I really enjoyed the concert last night.
She enjoys walking in the rain.
branchCoverage: derive or receive pleasure from -> get pleasure from something
get enjoyment from -> get pleasure from something
take pleasure in -> get pleasure from something

accepted.definition: constituting the undiminished entirety; lacking nothing essential especially not damaged
accepted.simpleMeaning: whole and complete, with nothing missing and nothing broken.
accepted.scope: It is not the everyday sense of 'all of' a period or group; it describes one object that is complete and undamaged.
examples: The ancient cup was found entire, with no cracks.
The museum's set of first editions is still entire.
branchCoverage: constituting the undiminished entirety -> whole and complete, with nothing missing
lacking nothing essential especially not damaged -> with nothing missing and nothing broken
accepted.lemmaPartition: entire (3 senses in this batch): adjective = whole and undamaged, with nothing missing (entire%5:00:02:whole:00); adjective = (of a leaf or petal) having a smooth edge (entire%5:00:00:smooth:02); adjective = including all of a group, area, or period (entire%5:00:01:whole:00).

accepted.definition: (of leaves or petals) having a smooth edge; not broken up into teeth or lobes
accepted.simpleMeaning: a leaf or petal with a smooth edge, not cut into teeth or deep rounded parts.
accepted.scope: It is not the everyday sense meaning whole or complete; it describes the shape of the edge of a leaf or petal.
examples: The bush has entire leaves with smooth edges.
Unlike oak leaves, these leaves are entire.
branchCoverage: (of leaves or petals) having a smooth edge -> a leaf or petal with a smooth edge
not broken up into teeth or lobes -> not cut into teeth or deep rounded parts
accepted.lemmaPartition: entire (3 senses in this batch): adjective = whole and undamaged, with nothing missing (entire%5:00:02:whole:00); adjective = (of a leaf or petal) having a smooth edge (entire%5:00:00:smooth:02); adjective = including all of a group, area, or period (entire%5:00:01:whole:00).

accepted.definition: constituting the full quantity or extent; complete
accepted.simpleMeaning: including every part of a group, area, or period, with nothing left out.
accepted.scope: It is not the sense of one object being unbroken or undamaged; it means all of a group, area, or period is included.
examples: She spent the entire day at the library.
The entire class passed the exam.
branchCoverage: constituting the full quantity or extent -> including every part of a group, area, or period
complete -> with nothing left out

accepted.definition: the destruction of an enemy plane or ship or tank or missile
accepted.simpleMeaning: an occasion when an enemy plane, ship, tank, or missile is destroyed.
accepted.scope: It is not the act of taking a person's life; it is a military count of destroyed enemy equipment.
examples: The pilot scored three kills in one mission.
The report listed the number of kills for the month.
branchCoverage: the destruction of an enemy plane or ship or tank or missile -> an occasion when an enemy plane, ship, tank, or missile is destroyed

accepted.definition: characterized by or indicating poverty
accepted.simpleMeaning: having very little money or few possessions.
accepted.scope: It is not the sense meaning bad in quality or deserving sympathy; it describes people or places that lack money.
examples: The charity helps poor families in the city.
He grew up in a poor neighbourhood with few shops.
branchCoverage: characterized by or indicating poverty -> having very little money or few possessions
